subject: How accurate cutting supports a better fit
hook: Track saw in the van, or panels arriving cut and edged? Most fitters we speak to do a bit of both.
ig:
Track saw in the van, or panels arriving cut and edged? Most fitters we speak to do a bit of both.

A: Cutting your own
Good for last-minute changes and one-off scribes. The catch is time, and keeping long cuts straight and corners square on a portable setup, especially across a full 2440 x 1220 sheet.

B: Ordering cut and edged panels
Panels come off a sliding table panel saw and an edge bander, so they arrive square with the ABS edging already applied. The catch is that you need a final cutting list before you order. Change your mind on site and you are back to option A.

Plenty of trade customers split it: carcass panels and long runs ordered in, fillers and scribes cut on site.

Which way do you work, and what is the one job that always makes you switch? Tell us in the comments.
fb:
A question for the joiners, fitters and cabinet makers who follow us around Stoke-on-Trent: do you cut your own boards, or have them sent out cut and edged?

Cutting your own gives you room to adjust when a wall is not quite what the drawing said. Ordering in saves hours at the saw and gives you square panels with the edging already on, but it only works with a final cutting list.

A lot of people do both: carcasses ordered in, fillers cut on site. What is your split? Let us know below, and if you fancy trying it with your next job, the details are here:
